title: Structural Valve Deterioration in End-Stage Renal Disease Patients With Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
authors: Berk Inan; Elizabeth M Cordoves; Gerardo Ramos-Lemos; Marco Tagliafierro; Ezra F Moos; Gift Owolabi; James Y Lao; Ian Mason; Ali Fatehi Hassanabad
abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) has revolutionized the management of aortic stenosis (AS), particularly for high-risk and inoperable populations. Nevertheless, patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) who require TAVR present a unique clinical challenge. These patients tend to have a high burden of comorbidities, as well as chronic uremia, that purportedly predispose them to a higher risk of more frequent and rapid structural valve deterioration (SVD). This narrative review synthesizes contemporary evidence regarding the mechanisms, incidence, and clinical outcomes of TAVR SVD in the ESRD population. In doing so, we summarize the pathophysiology for SVD in this patient population, contextualize the reported rates of TAVR SVD, and summarize the limited literature describing the clinical outcomes for these patients. We posit that clinical management for ESRD patients must focus on proactive, multidisciplinary surveillance and the integration of predictive modeling to optimize the timing of rescue interventions. Finally, we underscore the importance of better understanding the underlying mechanisms that accelerate TAVR SVD in uremic conditions.

title: Severe continuous prosthetic mitral regurgitation from chordal rupture after valve-sparing replacement: a case report.
authors: Hongxia Wang; Yun Mou; Jiabin Yuan
abstract:
After mitral valve replacement with preservation of the subvalvular apparatus, prosthetic dysfunction resulting from retained native structures is extremely rare. When it occurs, it may directly threaten the patient's life. We report an unusual case of severe regurgitation resulting from preserved chordal rupture. The key distinction of this case is the presentation of late, severe continuous prosthetic regurgitation and reversibility.
A 54-year-old man had undergone double mechanical valve replacement for severe rheumatic mitral stenosis with mild regurgitation and concomitant aortic regurgitation three years earlier. During surgery, the posterior mitral leaflet and its entire subvalvular apparatus were preserved. Current transesophageal echocardiography revealed a mobile, cord-like structure between the lateral occluder and the prosthetic sewing ring, interfering with leaflet excursion and preventing full closure. This was accompanied by severe prosthetic mitral continuous regurgitation. Surgical findings revealed a ruptured chordae tendineae at the papillary muscle attachment, with the remnant preventing leaflet coaptation. Surgical excision of the ruptured chordal remnant successfully restored normal leaflet function, with complete resolution of the regurgitation confirmed on intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography.
When obstruction or regurgitation develops after valve replacement with subvalvular preservation, uncommon causes-such as residual subvalvular tissue or ruptured chordal entrapment-should be considered after excluding more common etiologies. This case illustrates the critical role of transesophageal echocardiography in the diagnosis of chordal entrapment after mitral valve replacement and potentially in preventing complications. The potential benefit of preserving the subvalvular apparatus warrants thoughtful deliberation. Surgical removal of the offending tissue or valve replacement remains the definitive treatment.

title: [The predictive value of left ventricular strain on cardiac magnetic resonance for adverse events in children and adolescent patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy].
authors: X R Chen; X Ma; A X Zhang; Y Tang; K Yang; X Y Chen; S H Zhao
journal: Zhonghua xin xue guan bing za zhi
abstract: Objective: To investigate the role of left ventricular global longitudinal strain (GLS) derived from cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) feature-tracking in evaluating left ventricular systolic function in children and adolescents with primary hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), as well as its prognostic value for adverse cardiovascular events and heart failure-related events. Methods: This was a single-center retrospective cohort study. Patients with primary HCM aged ≤21 years who underwent standard CMR examination at Fuwai Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences, between January 2010 and December 2018 were included. Baseline clinical and CMR data were collected, and follow-up was completed. The primary endpoint was composite adverse cardiovascular events, and the secondary endpoint was heart failure-related events. Patients were divided into the event group and the non-event group according to whether the primary endpoint occurred. Multivariate Cox proportional-hazards regression models were used to identify independent factors associated with composite adverse cardiovascular events and heart failure-related events. Using the cohort median left ventricular GLS of -9.2% as the cut-off value, patients were stratified into the preserved GLS group (≤-9.2%) and the impaired GLS group (>-9.2%). Kaplan-Meier survival curves were plotted, and the log-rank test was performed to compare survival differences between groups. Results: A total of 249 children and adolescents with HCM were included, aged (14.81±3.71)years, of whom 163 were males (65.5%). The follow-up duration was (66.59±33.00)months. Composite endpoint events occurred in 37 patients, including 17 heart failure-related events and 20 sudden cardiac death events; 212 patients remained event-free. After adjusting for confounders such as left ventricular ejection fraction and history of unexplained syncope, multivariate Cox regression demonstrated that the percentage of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) and left ventricular GLS were independently associated with composite adverse cardiovascular events (left ventricular GLS: HR=1.18, 95%CI 1.04-1.35, P=0.014; LGE extent: HR=1.12, 95%CI 1.06-1.18,P<0.001) and heart failure-related events (left ventricular GLS: HR=1.52, 95%CI 1.18-1.96, P=0.001; LGE extent: HR=1.14, 95%CI 1.04-1.24, P=0.003). Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed that patients with impaired left ventricular GLS had lower cumulative event-free survival for both composite adverse cardiovascular events and heart failure-related events compared with those with preserved GLS (log-rank all P<0.001). Conclusions: CMR feature-tracking can effectively assess left ventricular systolic function in children and adolescents with primary HCM. Left ventricular GLS and LGE percentage are independently associated with the risk of adverse cardiovascular events and heart failure-related events in this patient population.

title: Echocardiographic predictors of left ventricular ejection fraction improvement after transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
authors: Shin Sato; Akiko Kumagai; Kai Ninomiya; Akiko Murofushi; Kaho Shimada; Michiko Yoshizawa; Ryo Ninomiya; Tetsuya Fusazaki; Yoshihiro Morino
abstract:
Improvement in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) has been associated with better clinical outcomes, but predictors of recovery remain poorly defined. This study aimed to identify echocardiographic parameters associated with post-TAVR LVEF improvement in patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS) and reduced LVEF.
Among 1,133 consecutive patients who underwent TAVR between December 2013 and June 2024, 128 with baseline LVEF < 50% and follow-up echocardiography within 3 months were analyzed. LVEF improvement was defined as an absolute increase ≥ 10%. Independent predictors were identified using multivariable logistic regression. Post-procedural outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis.
LVEF improvement occurred in 64 patients (50%). Multivariable analysis identified higher left ventricular mass index (LVMI) (OR 1.02, 95% CI 1.00-1.03, P = 0.01) and higher E/e' (OR 1.10, 95% CI 1.03-1.18, P < 0.01) as independent predictors of improvement, whereas larger left ventricular end-diastolic volume (LVEDV) (OR 0.98, P = 0.01) and larger AVA (OR 0.67 per 0.1 cm², P < 0.01) were inversely associated. Patients with LVEF improvement had significantly lower 1-year all-cause mortality (98.2% vs. 87.0%, P = 0.01).
Echocardiographic parameters reflecting pressure overload and diastolic dysfunction predict LVEF recovery after TAVR. Postoperative LVEF improvement was associated with better 1-year survival, underscoring its prognostic value.

title: Feasibility and outcomes of long-segment tracheal replacement with biological and engineered scaffolds.
authors: Qiang Su; Daichen Liu; Ying Han
abstract:
To synthesize adult long-segment tracheal replacement using a combined anatomical and graft-based framework and to compare clinically established and investigational strategies with emphasis on mortality, morbidity, airway function, and reintervention.
PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure were searched from January 1, 2000, to June 30, 2026. Adult replacements were classified as Type I (upper/cervical), Type II (cervico-mediastinal), Type III (intrathoracic), or Type IV (distal trachea/carina) and by graft class. Forty-three reports comprising 147 extractable patients were synthesized descriptively. The overlapping 50-patient TRITON-01 registry was analyzed separately as the principal cryopreserved aortic-allograft benchmark.
Among 147 patients, 72 were Type I, 33 Type II, 25 Type III, and 17 Type IV; 113 (76.9%) had malignant disease. Autologous vascularized tissue composites were used in 74 patients (50.3%) and cryopreserved aortic allografts in 52 (35.4%). Overall 30-day and 90-day mortality were 4.8% and 9.5%, respectively. Decannulation was achieved in 103/139 (74.1%); 25.2% required repeat endoscopic intervention and 19.0% developed recurrent stenosis. In the updated 50-patient TRITON-01 registry, 30-day mortality was 4%, major complications 30%, stent-related granuloma 52%, and stent removal 30%. Reliable Type I-IV-specific mortality rates could not be pooled because primary reports did not consistently cross-tabulate outcomes by anatomical level.
Anatomy should precede material choice when interpreting tracheal replacement. Autologous vascularized composites have the most mature experience for selected Type I-II reconstruction, whereas Type III-IV intrathoracic and distal/carinal replacement remains more technically hazardous. Cryopreserved aortic allografts provide the current clinical benchmark for biologic full-circumference replacement but require structured stent and bronchoscopic management. Tracheal allotransplantation and engineered or xenogenic constructs remain limited or investigational.

title: Early and Mid-Term Mortality After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: Five-Year Experience from the KOSUTAVI Study.
authors: Regayip Zehir; Elnur Alizade; Songül Usalp; Mehmet Yunus Emiroğlu; Ramazan Kargın; Nihal Özdemir; Cevat Kırma; Cihangir Kaymaz; Mehmet Muhsin Türkmen; Selçuk Pala; Şeyhmus Külahçıoğlu; Mehmet Kaan Kırali
abstract:
Although transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) outcomes are well-documented, predictors of mortality beyond conventional surgical risk scores and valve-related factors in real-world, high-risk cohorts require further elucidation. This study aimed to identify the key determinants of 30-day and 1-year mortality following TAVI, with a focus on both patient-specific and procedure-specific complications.
The KOSUTAVI study is a single-center, retrospective cohort analysis of 859 consecutive high-risk individuals with severe aortic stenosis undergoing TAVI between 2020 and 2025. Primary endpoints were 30-day and 1-year all-cause mortality. Multivariate Cox regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses were used to identify independent risk factors.
Mean age was 78.7 ± 6.5 years, and mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons score was 7.4 ± 2.2. The 30-day and 1-year mortality rates were 6.5% (n = 56) and 12.4% (n = 107), respectively. The 5-year all-cause mortality rate was 26.3%. In multiple Cox's analysis, chronic renal failure (hazard ratio [HR] = 7.75, P = .008, 95% CI = 1.29-16.54), presentation with cardiogenic shock (HR = 5.83, P = .028, 95% CI = 1.19-15.41), major vascular injury (HR = 22.7, P = .019, 95% CI = 1.89-45.91), and cardiac tamponade (HR = 17.9, P = .012, 95% CI = 8.13-52.62) were independently associated with 30-day mortality. While these factors were all significant in univariate analysis for 1-year mortality, they did not retain independence in the multiple model. Valve type, access route, and sex were not associated with increased mortality.
In a high-risk TAVI population, early mortality is predominantly driven by pre-existing renal dysfunction and acute procedural complications (shock, vascular injury, and tamponade), rather than valve-specific factors. These findings underscore the critical importance of optimizing renal function before the procedure and implementing advanced vascular protection strategies to improve early survival after TAVI.

title: Multimodal Atrial Cardiomyopathy Phenotypes for Risk Stratification in Severe Aortic Stenosis Undergoing TAVI.
authors: Raffaella Mistrulli; Emiliano Fiori; Tatiana Storozhenko; Sara Corradetti; Anthony Kechichian; Nikolaos Stalikas; Dimitri Buytaert; Davide Ausiello; Michele Mattia Viscusi; Pasquale Paolisso; Marta Belmonte; Emanuele Gallinoro; Jerremy Weerts; Emanuele Barbato; Guy Van Camp; Martin Penicka; Eric Wyffels; Marc Vanderheyden
abstract:
Atrial cardiomyopathy (AtCM) is highly prevalent in patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS), even in the presence of preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). Structural, functional, and electrical atrial remodeling may differentially influence outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), although their integrated prognostic role remains unclear.
To assess whether multimodal markers of AtCM identify distinct risk phenotypes associated with adverse outcomes after TAVI in patients without prior atrial fibrillation (AF).
We retrospectively analyzed 122 consecutive patients with severe AS, preserved LVEF, and sinus rhythm undergoing TAVI. Structural/functional AtCM (Echo-AtCM Risk) was assessed using indexed left atrial volume (LAVI) and left atrial reservoir strain (LASr), whereas electrical AtCM (ECG-AtCM Risk) was defined according to P-wave duration and morphology. Patients were followed for all-cause mortality, heart failure (HF) hospitalization, and new-onset AF. Prognostic associations were evaluated using multivariable Cox regression analyses.
Mean age was 82.3±5.6 years. High Echo-Risk was present in 54.1% of patients and High ECG-Risk in 19.7%. During a median follow-up of 13.6 months, the composite endpoint of all-cause mortality or HF hospitalization occurred in 39 patients (32.0%), while new-onset AF developed in 17 (13.9%). High Echo-Risk independently predicted death/HF hospitalization (HR 4.17, p=0.008), whereas High ECG-Risk independently predicted incident AF (HR 3.07, p=0.034). Combined profiling identified distinct phenotypes: High Echo/Low ECG predicted HF/death (HR 4.86, p=0.008), Low Echo/High ECG predicted AF (HR 8.99, p=0.004), and combined High Echo/High ECG conferred the worst prognosis (HR 6.23, p=0.015).
Structural, functional, and electrical AtCM represent complementary domains with distinct prognostic implications in AS patients undergoing TAVI. Their integration may refine post-TAVI risk stratification; these exploratory findings require external validation before clinical management can be guided by AtCM phenotype.Keywords: Atrial cardiomyopathy; Aortic stenosis; TAVI; Left atrial strain; Heart failure; Atrial fibrillation.

title: The Senokine Gas6 Promotes Aortic Valve Calcification Through CaMKII-DRP1-Mediated Terminal Scission of Mitochondrial-Derived Vesicles.
authors: Yaoyu Zhang; Jialiang Zhang; Yanjiani Xu; Wenhua Lei; Fei Xu; Junli Li; Zisong Wei; Bo Su; Shuang Liu; Jing Zhou; Hongde Li; Junpeng Ran; Weiya Li; Tuerhongjiang Tuerdi; Xiaojiao Wang; Zhi Fang; Fangyang Huang; Mao Chen
abstract: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is an age-associated valvular disorder in which calcification expands from discrete foci into adjacent tissue. We investigated whether mitochondrial-derived vesicles (MDVs) released by human valvular interstitial cells (hVICs) exert pro-calcific effects on recipient cells and how MDV release is regulated. Using ex vivo hemodynamic perfusion of human CAVD tissue, multi-omics profiling, live-cell single-organelle tracking, MDV transfer assays, and in vivo Gas6 deletion, we found that calcifying hVICs hypersecreted MDVs that exerted pro-calcific effects in recipient hVICs. High-resolution imaging showed that mitochondria remodeled into donut-shaped structures under pro-osteogenic conditions; these structures served as physical platforms for MDV budding. Human CAVD valve tissues and hVICs treated with pro-osteogenic medium also exhibited senescence-associated features. Multi-omics profiling identified growth arrest-specific 6 (Gas6), a senokine, among 36 concordantly upregulated candidates. Functional analyzes showed that Gas6 promoted terminal MDV scission while leaving donut-shaped mitochondrial precursor formation intact. Mechanistically, Gas6 promoted intracellular Ca2+ accumulation, calcium/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII) activation, and dynamin-related protein 1 (DRP1) phosphorylation at Ser616, supporting a Ca2+-CaMKII-DRP1 axis that facilitates terminal MDV scission. Pharmacological inhibition of CaMKII or DRP1 reduced MDV hypersecretion and subsequent recipient-cell calcification, and Gas6 deletion in vivo attenuated valvular stenosis, calcification, and fibrotic remodeling. These findings identify Gas6-dependent terminal MDV scission as a mechanism contributing to the intercellular propagation of valvular calcification in a CAVD context characterized by senescence-associated features.

title: Stenosis of a novel frozen elephant trunk in a patient with chronic dissection.
authors: Shigeto Tokunaga; Homare Okamura; Atsushi Yamaguchi
abstract: A partial elephant trunk (PET), a new type of frozen elephant trunk, was designed to prevent distal stent graft-induced new entry using a thinner nitinol wire with less radial force. We report a case of PET stenosis in chronic dissection. Total arch replacement was performed using a PET. After weaning from cardiopulmonary bypass, the lower-limb blood pressure decreased to 90% of the upper-limb blood pressure. Intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography revealed incomplete PET expansion, and on postoperative day 1, the lower-to-upper body blood pressure ratio further decreased to 70% due to PET stenosis at the steeply angulated arch. Emergency thoracic endovascular aortic repair was successfully performed, completely resolving the pressure gradient.

title: Intravascular Lithotripsy of Aortic and Renal Lesions as a Therapeutic Tool for Pickering Syndrome: A Case Report.
authors: Miguel Martínez-Cachero García; Carlos Ariza Molina; Susana Ana Sanmartino González; Amer Zanabili Al-Sibbai
abstract: We report the case of a 73-year-old woman admitted with Pickering syndrome, a life-threatening condition characterized by recurrent flash pulmonary edema secondary to severe renovascular disease. Computed tomography angiography demonstrated an atrophic left kidney, a heavily calcified visceral aorta with a coral-reef morphology, and a near-occlusive stenosis of the right renal artery. Urgent endovascular treatment was performed with intravascular lithotripsy for plaque modification of the suprarenal aorta and the right renal artery, followed by renal artery stenting. The patient showed prompt clinical recovery, with resolution of pulmonary edema, stabilization of blood pressure, and improvement of renal function. This case illustrates the potential role of intravascular lithotripsy as a minimally invasive adjunct for managing severely calcified aorto-renal disease in high-risk patients, enabling endovascular treatment in otherwise challenging anatomy.

title: Crystalloid vs colloid for Hemodynamics during Anesthesia INduction in TAVR patients (CHAIN-T): study protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
authors: Xiaoshuang Tuo; Fahan Wang; Youjun Chen; Min Chen; Zhihong Lu
abstract:
To assess whether preload with colloids could reduce hypotension during induction in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) compared to crystalloids.
This study is a single-center, prospective, randomized, double-blind, parallel-controlled trial conducted at Xijing Hospital. A total of 116 patients scheduled for elective TAVR under general anesthesia will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either the colloid group or the crystalloid group, receiving either 5 ml/kg of colloid or crystalloid solution before anesthesia induction infused over 15 min. The primary outcome is the area under curve (AUC) of the change in mean arterial pressure (MAP) from baseline during the induction period (until 15 min after induction). Secondary outcomes include the incidence of intraoperative hemodynamic instability, the use of intraoperative vasoactive drugs, the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score on the first postoperative day, postoperative hospital length of stay, the rate of intensive care unit (ICU) admission postoperatively, all-cause mortality during hospitalization and by 30 days after surgery, and the incidence of renal replacement therapy by 30 days after surgery.
The results of this study will provide evidence on optimizing fluid preload to prevent hypotension during induction, reduce postoperative complications, and enhance recovery for patients undergoing TAVR. The findings are expected to promote anesthesia protocols in this patient population.
The study protocol and statistical analysis plan were approved by the institutional Ethics Committee of Xijing Hospital, Fourth Military Medical University (XJLL-KY-20252560). The study was registered in ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07329660) on December 29, 2025.

title: Neurological manifestations and vasculopathy in PLCG2-associated antibody deficiency and immune dysregulation (APLAID): a case series.
authors: Kosar Asna Ashari; Rebecca MacRae; David P Hoytema van Konijnenburg; Craig D Platt; Maryam Ashoor; Alfred P See; Agnieszka Kielian; Amy Danehy; Riten Kumar; Elliot James; Kristin Houghton; Sheri Harder; Mark P Gorman; Stacy A Kahn; Ankana Daga; Sadaf H Hussain; Alicia M Johnston; Alicia Casey; Jodie D Ouahed; Wai Wong; Kathy Jenkins; Susan Prockop; Esraa Eloseily; Kimberly Risma; Michael J Ombrello; Fatma Dedeoglu; Milena M Andzelm
abstract:
Autosomal dominant pathogenic variants in PLCG2 are associated with autoinflammation and PLCG2-associated antibody deficiency and immune dysregulation (APLAID), characterized by immunological abnormalities and multi-system inflammation. Descriptions of associated neurological manifestations and vascular anomalies are limited. We describe three patients with APLAID, vasculopathies, neuroinflammation, and cerebral vascular tortuosity. These cases highlight underrecognized and clinically important manifestations of APLAID.
All three patients had de novo variants in PLCG2 and early systemic inflammatory and immunodeficiency findings within the spectrum of APLAID (e.g. immune laboratory abnormalities, skin and gastrointestinal inflammation, and frequent infections). Additionally, they had notable neurological and vascular findings. Patient #1 (PLCG2 c.3420T > A; p.Asp1140Glu) is a female who had focal seizures at 16 months old. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed right parietal leptomeningeal enhancement with white matter changes. MR angiography (MRA) showed cerebrovascular tortuosity and stenoses without evidence of vasculitis. She had extensive veno-lymphatic malformation in the thorax, abnormal renal vasculature, inferior vena cava (IVC) atresia, and bilateral pulmonary vein stenosis (PVS). Patient #2 (PLCG2 c.2122G > C; p.Ala708Pro) is a male who at four years old had an episode of status epilepticus. MRI revealed a right parietal infarct with surrounding leptomeningeal enhancement and MRA demonstrated abnormal caliber of the right middle cerebral artery (MCA), arterial tortuosity, and carotid aneurysms. His course was complicated by aortic root dilation and bilateral PVS. Patient #3 (PLCG2 c.2122G > C; p.Ala708Pro) is a male who at 16 months had a right sided focal motor seizure. MRI demonstrated infarct with associated sulcal enhancement predominantly in the left cerebral hemisphere. MRA found excessive vascular tortuosity and fenestrations. He has a dilated aortic root and ventricular septal defect (VSD).
We present three cases of APLAID complicated by significant cerebrovascular tortuosity and seizure and two with cerebral ischemia. The etiology of stroke and/or seizures in these patients is unclear, but vasculopathy leading to perfusion deficits, neuroinflammation, or thrombosis due to underlying thrombotic diathesis or abnormal vascular anatomy may have contributed. We recommend all patients with APLAID undergo monitoring for neurologic manifestations. Additionally, we highlight important vasculopathic findings such as PVS, where early recognition for directed treatment is critical.

title: Refractory rapidly progressive diffuse in-stent restenosis with left main involvement: a case report.
authors: Xiaoyan Wang; Haichao Yang; Liqiang Qin; Wei Lu; Lijun Wang; Jianjun Wang; Juan Li; Kaibin Deng; Chenguang Gao
abstract:
Drug-eluting stents (DES) have significantly reduced the incidence of in-stent restenosis (ISR). However, a subset of patients still develop refractory, rapidly progressive, and diffuse ISR, which poses substantial therapeutic challenges and reflects its complex underlying mechanisms.
We report a 46-year-old male who underwent five percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI) over five years, with repeated diffuse ISR in the left anterior descending artery (LAD). Initial PCI was followed by DCB therapy after first ISR, achieving temporary symptom relief. Four years later, ISR progressed to chronic total occlusion, requiring further stenting and DCB therapy. Within five months, he developed 99% LM stenosis and recurrent LAD ISR. Despite a SYNTAX score of 36 favoring CABG, the patient refused surgery. Under intra-aortic balloon pump support, a balloon-only PCI (stent-less) strategy was performed. IVUS revealed diffuse fibrous proliferation and neoatherosclerosis. During follow-up, the patient remained clinically stable overall.
This case highlights a potential systemic hyperproliferative phenotype, in which repeated vascular injury triggers accelerated neoatherosclerosis and intimal hyperplasia. It challenges the conventional view of ISR as a local mechanical problem and underscores the importance of mechanism-driven risk stratification and individualized management, particularly when standard surgical therapy is declined.

title: Discharge NT-proBNP predicts 2-year outcomes after TAVR but not after SAVR in preserved ejection fraction: a propensity-matched cohort study.
authors: Hua-Jie Zheng; Ling-Ling Zeng; Mei Guo; Chao-Jun Yan; Rui-Han Xiao; Xiao-Qing Tang; Yong-Bo Cheng; Ya-Nan Wei; Wei Cheng
abstract:
Discharge N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) is a recognised prognostic marker after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), but its value after surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) remains uncertain, possibly reflecting differences in perioperative physiology.
To compare the prognostic utility of discharge NT-proBNP after TAVR versus SAVR in patients with severe aortic stenosis and preserved ejection fraction, and to examine the association between NT-proBNP reduction and Left Ventricular Mass Index (LVMI) regression.
This propensity-matched cohort study included 556 patients (TAVR, n=278; SAVR, n=278) with left ventricular ejection fraction ≥50% treated at a single centre (2019–2023). The primary endpoint was a 2-year composite of all-cause death or heart failure rehospitalisation.
After matching, baseline characteristics were well balanced. Discharge NT-proBNP >1000 pg/mL predicted lower event-free survival after TAVR (77.3% vs 91.4%; adjusted HR 3.21, 95% CI 1.96 to 5.26, p<0.001) but not after SAVR (83.8% vs 86.7%; adjusted HR 1.18, p=0.50; p for interaction=0.008). Longer aortic cross-clamp time progressively abolished NT-proBNP prognostic value in SAVR. NT-proBNP reduction correlated with LVMI regression regardless of procedure (β=2.2 per 10% ΔNT-proBNP%, p<0.001). A 6-month NT-proBNP ≤1000 pg/mL identified favourable outcomes irrespective of procedure (adjusted HR 0.51, p=0.002).
Discharge NT-proBNP predicts outcomes after TAVR but not SAVR, likely due to cardiopulmonary bypass-induced inflammation. NT-proBNP reduction correlates with LVMI regression irrespective of procedure. Risk stratification may be optimised by discharge measurement after TAVR and 6-month reassessment after SAVR.

title: Atrial Fibrillation in Valvular Heart Disease: Assessing the Impact of Genetics in the UK Biobank.
authors: Luca Cristin; Janet J Tang; Lionel Tastet; Rohit Jhawar; David V Glidden; Gregory M Marcus; Francesca N Delling
abstract:
Atrial fibrillation (AF) in valvular heart disease (VHD) is generally attributed to pressure or volume overload with atrial remodeling, but the independent contribution of genetic predisposition remains unclear.
The authors evaluated the predictive value of a previously developed AF polygenic risk score (PRS) across VHD subtypes in the UK Biobank.
In this prospective cohort study (UK Biobank, 2000-2022), incident AF and VHD status were defined using ICD codes. VHD subtypes included mitral valve (MV) disease (MV prolapse [MVP], mitral regurgitation, mitral stenosis) and aortic valve (AV) disease (aortic stenosis, aortic regurgitation). PRS was categorized into quintiles and grouped as low, intermediate, and high.
Among 452,841 participants with available PRS, 385 had MVP, 1,058 mitral regurgitation, 81 mitral stenosis, 421 aortic regurgitation, and 509 aortic stenosis. In Cox models, PRS was independently associated with incident AF in MV disease (HR: 1.7, P = 0.03 for intermediate PRS; HR: 2.3, P = 0.002 for high PRS), with the strongest effect in MVP (HR: 3.1, P = 0.03 for high PRS). In AV disease, PRS was not significantly associated with AF risk (P = 0.93 and P = 0.07 for intermediate and high PRS, respectively). Interaction analyses confirmed attenuation or absence of the PRS effect in AV disease (P = 0.04 and P = 0.004 for intermediate and high PRS, respectively), whereas no significant interaction was observed in MV disease (P = 0.80 and P = 0.11, respectively).
In VHD, AF PRS predicts AF risk, but the genetic impact differs by subtype. AV disease shows minimal genetic contribution, suggesting predominantly hemodynamic risk, while MV disease-particularly MVP-shows substantial genetic influence.

title: Impact of Coronary Artery Disease on Long-Term Valve Function After the Ozaki Procedure: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study (2015 - 2020).
authors: Vladlen Bazylev; Artur Mikulyak; Khadiev M Dzhokhar; Yazan Khanfar; Vadim Karnakhin
abstract:
The Ozaki procedure reconstructs the aortic valve with autologous pericardium, but long-term leaflet durability remains uncertain. Coronary artery disease (CAD) may reflect a systemic atheroinflammatory milieu associated with impaired leaflet integrity.
We retrospectively studied 733 patients undergoing Ozaki reconstruction from 2015 to 2020 and assessed the association between CAD and aortic regurgitation (AR) ≥ 2 at last echocardiographic follow-up. Baseline heterogeneity was addressed using propensity-score overlap weighting based on age, sex, body mass index, body surface area, weight, diabetes, European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation II, aortic stenosis, bicuspid valve, and peripheral artery disease. Effects were estimated as weighted risk ratios (RRs) using Poisson models with robust variance. Sensitivity analyses used stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and an extended model including prior myocardial infarction/percutaneous coronary intervention.
Of 733 patients, 365 (49.8%) had CAD. Unadjusted AR > 2 rates were 10.1% in CAD vs. 5.7% in no-CAD patients (P = 0.037). After overlap weighting, weighted risks were 12.7% vs. 6.2%, yielding RR 2.05 (95% CI, 1.01 - 4.18; P = 0.048), with excellent covariate balance. IPTW showed consistent results: RR 2.22 (95% CI, 1.38 - 3.56; P = 0.001). Regurgitation-free survival was lower in CAD patients (log-rank P = 0.0087).
CAD was associated with an approximately two-fold higher risk of AR ≥ 2 after Ozaki reconstruction. This association likely reflects systemic atheroinflammatory processes rather than a direct mechanical effect, supporting closer postoperative surveillance in CAD patients.

title: Diagnostic performance of aortic valve calcium and CT-derived aortic valve area in low-gradient aortic stenosis.
authors: Dakota De Cecco; Christopher Scoma; Corey Powell; Megan Joseph; William Truesdell; Stanley Chetcuti; Andrew W Harris
abstract:
Practice guidelines recommend the use of computed tomography (CT) aortic valve calcium (AVC) scores for patients with low-gradient aortic stenosis (LG-AS). AVC has not been studied in comparison to invasive aortic valve study (IAVS).
To determine the diagnostic performance of AVC and CT-derived aortic valve area (CT-AVA) compared to IAVS as a reference standard.
We included consecutive patients with LG-AS with echocardiography, CT and IAVS performed within 1 year at a single tertiary center. Severe AS was defined by aortic valve area (AVA) ≤1.0 cm2 measured by IAVS. CT-AVA was retrospectively measured by a blinded reader. CT-AVA and sex-based AVC were compared to AS defined by IAVS. Diagnostic performance was compared using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. AVC and CT-AVA were compared to cardiac events consisting of death, aortic valve replacement and cardiovascular hospitalization.
Out of 294 patients in the overall cohort, 206 patients with definite AS severity by IAVS were included as the primary diagnostic cohort. Severe AS according to invasive AVA (≤1.0 cm2) was present in 72 patients (35.0%). Sex-based AVC scores had relatively poor diagnostic performance compared to the reference IAVS with AUCs of 0.59 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.48-0.70) and 0.58 (95% CI 0.45-0.71) for men and women, respectively. CT-AVA had better diagnostic performance with an AUC of 0.82 (95% CI 0.77-0.87).
In our study population, CT-AVA had significantly better diagnostic performance than AVC compared to the reference standard, IAVS.

title: EFFECTIVENESS OF TOTAL ARTERIAL REVASCULARIZATION COMPARED TO SAPHENOUS VEIN GRAFT IN MULTIVESSEL CORONARY ARTERY BYPASS SURGERY : A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIALS AND PRIMARY STUDIES
authors: I GNA Bayu Wiradinatha; I Made Indra Prasetya
journal: The Indonesian Journal of General Medicine
abstract: Introduction: Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) remains the preferred revascularisation strategy for complex multivessel coronary artery disease, yet the great saphenous vein graft (SVG) is still used in the vast majority of operations despite its progressive late attrition. Total arterial revascularization (TAR), the complete avoidance of SVG, has been proposed to eliminate vein-graft failure, but its superiority rests largely on observational data. This review synthesised contemporary (2021-2026) randomised and primary evidence comparing TAR, or arterial-for-venous conduit substitution, with SVG-containing CABG.1–3 Methods: The study strictly adhered to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines. Randomised controlled trials (RCTs), prospective and retrospective cohort, case-control and cross-sectional studies comparing TAR (or an arterial conduit replacing SVG) with SVG-containing CABG in multivessel disease were eligible. Results: Twenty-one reports (3 RCTs; 18 observational reports from 15 cohorts; 18 unique cohorts; approximately 73,700 patients from 14 countries) were included. In non-randomised cohorts, TAR was associated with lower long-term all-cause mortality (5 independent estimates; HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.76-0.99; p = 0.041; I² = 35.4%), but the association lost significance after HKSJ adjustment (95% CI 0.71-1.06) and the prediction interval crossed unity (0.61-1.24). Randomised comparisons of arterial versus venous conduits to the second target showed no mortality difference (HR 0.93, 0.62-1.40; I² = 75.2%), although RAPCO-SV demonstrated fewer 15-year major adverse cardiac events (HR 0.71, 0.52-0.98). Across all seven estimates the pooled HR was 0.89 (0.78-1.03). Within the Australian and New Zealand registry, the benefit was consistent in men (HR 0.86) and women (0.82), in patients aged 70 years or older (0.87) and younger (0.80), but not demonstrable when LVEF was below 30% (0.87, 0.67-1.13). Early outcomes favoured TAR in small cohorts (in-hospital death/MACCE RR 0.35, 0.15-0.80), with shorter ventilation, intensive care and hospital stay. No small-study effect was detected (Egger p = 0.91). Certainty of evidence was low to very low.8–13 Discussion: The survival signal favouring TAR is modest, driven predominantly by one large binational registry, susceptible to residual confounding and surgeon-selection bias, and is not confirmed by randomised conduit trials; conversely, no signal of harm emerged, and arterial strategies appeared safe with favourable perioperative profiles in experienced centres. Benefit appears most plausible in patients with long life expectancy and high-grade non-LAD target stenoses.2,14,15 Conclusion: Contemporary evidence supports TAR as a safe strategy associated with a modest long-term survival advantage in observational data, but high-certainty proof of superiority over SVG-containing CABG is lacking. Individualised conduit selection by an experienced heart team is recommended pending adequately powered RCTs such as the Total Arterial (TA) Trial.1,3

title: Exploring the application value of preoperative femoral artery and vein cannulation in redo cardiac surgery
authors: Yi Hui Yu; Xun Li Zhang; Lei Wang; Li Qiong Xiao; Fu Hua Huang; Zhen Hong Wang
abstract: To explore the clinical value of preoperative femoral vessel cannulation in redo cardiac surgery. A retrospective analysis was performed on the clinical data of 106 patients who underwent redo cardiac surgery in our hospital from January 2022 to December 2024. According to the cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) cannulation technique adopted, the patients were divided into the Femoral Cannulation group (n = 79) and the Traditional Central Cannulation group (n = 37). Preoperative baseline data, intraoperative CPB-related parameters, blood product consumption, and the incidence of postoperative complications were recorded and compared between the two groups. There were no statistically significant differences in preoperative baseline data or intraoperative parameters between the two groups (all P > 0.05). Similarly, no significant statistical differences were found in postoperative mortality, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) utilization rate, acute kidney injury (AKI) incidence, or cognitive dysfunction incidence between the two groups. However, compared with the Traditional Central Cannulation group, the Femoral Cannulation group had significantly lower intraoperative packed red blood cell (PRBC) transfusion volume and a significantly lower incidence of major cardiovascular injuries (all P < 0.05). In redo cardiac surgery, preoperative femoral vessel cannulation can significantly reduce the incidence of major cardiovascular injuries and the demand for intraoperative blood transfusion, which is worthy of promotion and application in clinical practice.

title: Challenging the guidelines: longitudinal trends in left ventricular diameter and function in severe aortic regurgitation
authors: Shmuel Schwartzenberg; Amit Berkowitz; Tsahi T. Lerman; Tamir Bental; Mordehay Vaturi; Yair Goldberg; Yaron Shapira
abstract: Background Guidelines recommend aortic valve replacement (AVR) in patients with severe aortic regurgitation (AR) based on progressive changes in left ventricular (LV) function or size. We aimed to reassess the clinical relevance of current guideline recommendations pertaining to traditional echocardiographic measurements in routine practice. Methods Retrospective analysis of patients with severe AR who underwent serial echocardiographic follow-up over at least 18 months. The composite outcome was symptom-driven AVR, acute heart failure hospitalization, or death. We used a joint modelling approach to handle within-subject correlation and censoring. Results The cohort consisted of 140 patients, with a median follow-up of 93 months (interquartile range 58–130). LV end-systolic (LVESD) and fractional shortening (FS) showed a small but statistically significant longitudinal trend, while LVEDD did not. In three separate joint models adjusted for age at onset and sex, higher LVESD and LVEDD and lower FS were each associated with increased risk of the composite event. Each 1 mm increase in LVESD and LVEDD was associated with a 6% in risk; each 1% decrease in FS corresponded to a 12% increase in risk. Only 8 (5.7%) of patients were predicted to exceed the guideline-recommended LVEDD threshold of 65 mm over 10 years. Age at onset was also a significant risk factor, with each decade increasing risk by 65% for each of the three parallel joint models. Conclusion LV parameters show modest changes over time, despite holding strong prognostic value in patients with severe AR. LVEDD, while associated with overall risk, does not predictably or significantly dilate over time in most patients. AVR decisions should be based on comprehensive clinical and volumetric assessment rather than waiting for simple linear progression to guideline cutoffs.

title: Protein lactylation in atherosclerosis – Mechanisms and therapeutic potential: A narrative review
authors: Lijuan Zou; Yingquan Zhu; Yining Lan; Yiheng Cheng; Bing Han; Jinglian Chen; Chao Qin; Daobin Cheng
abstract: Protein lactylation, which links cellular metabolism to gene regulation and protein function, may influence atherosclerosis. This narrative review explores its cellular mechanisms and therapeutic potential. We searched PubMed from inception to September 30, 2026, for English-language studies and reviews. The synthesis differentiated lactylation from lactate signaling and distinguished direct evidence in atherosclerosis from findings in other disease models. Predominantly preclinical evidence suggests that both histone and non-histone lactylation are involved in endothelial inflammation, endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition, macrophage polarization and ferroptosis, and vascular smooth muscle cell senescence, phenotypic remodeling, and calcification. Depending on the cellular context, modification site, and downstream targets, lactylation can either promote vascular injury or support anti-inflammatory responses and plaque stabilization. Candidate interventions target lactate production, transport, and lactylation-related enzymes, but their effects often lack specificity for lactylation. Much of the therapeutic evidence originates from non-atherosclerotic models, and clinical validation is currently absent. Therefore, therapeutic development should consider cell type, disease stage, and modification site, with validation of causal mechanisms, selectivity, and safety in atherosclerosis models prior to clinical translation.

title: Occurrence and Antenatal Detection of Congenital Heart Malformations: Data from a Tertiary Obstetric Centre in Western Romania
authors: Adrian Ciulpan; Adrian Lăcătuşu; Liviu Laurentiu Pop; Corina Paul; Daniela Iacob; Brenda-Cristiana Bernad; Maghet Edida; Lucian Șerbănescu; Andrada-Ioana Dumitru; Monica Simina Mihuţa; Elena Silvia Bernad
abstract: Introduction: Congenital heart defects (CHDs) are the most frequent group of major congenital anomalies and impose a disproportionate burden on neonatal services. Antenatal detection determines where and how an affected newborn is delivered, yet reported detection rates differ several-fold between European countries. We aimed to quantify the postnatal occurrence and the antenatal detection of CHDs in a tertiary obstetric center in Western Romania and to place both figures in a comparable international context. Material and Methods: Retrospective observational study of all 10,113 births registered at the “Pius Brînzeu” County Clinical Emergency Hospital, Timișoara, between 2018 and 2022. Newborns with at least one cardiac lesion recorded on indication-based postnatal echocardiography were identified from the hospital electronic record. Interatrial communications and ductal patency recorded at the neonatal-index examination were counted inclusively and are analyzed separately from structural defects. A defect was classified as antenatally detected when it had been reported at any prenatal ultrasound scan and was subsequently confirmed postnatally. Proportions are reported with Wilson score 95% confidence intervals (CIs), separately at the level of the newborn and at the level of the individual lesion. Results: A total of 541 newborns carried at least one recorded cardiac lesion, giving an occurrence of 5.35% of births (95% CI 4.93–5.81); 670 individual lesions were recorded, a mean of 1.24 per affected newborn. Interatrial communication (n = 319; 47.6% of lesions) and ductal patency (n = 90; 13.4%) accounted for 61.0% of lesions; among the 261 structural defects, ventricular-septal defect was the most frequent (n = 121; 46.4%). An antenatal diagnosis had been made in 151 of 541 newborns (27.9%; 95% CI 24.3–31.8). Detection was highest for lesions distorting the four-chamber view, hypoplastic left-heart syndrome 4/5, and ventricular septal defect 80/121 (66.1%; 95% CI 57.3–73.9), and lowest for lesions requiring outflow-tract or arch views, including pulmonary stenosis 3/27 (11.1%; 95% CI 3.9–28.1) and aortic stenosis 0/12. Restricting the count to structural defects gives 13.1 to 25.8 affected newborns per 1000 births, against a EUROCAT total prevalence of 8.0 per 1000. Conclusions: The occurrence recorded here reflects tertiary referral, indication-based echocardiography, and an inclusive case definition rather than a genuine population excess, and is not interchangeable with registry prevalence. The antenatal detection rate of 27.9% sits between European settings without organized screening and those performing two or three routine scans per pregnancy. The detection deficit is concentrated in lesions that require outflow-tract or arch views. Because the views obtained at each scan were not recorded and detection was not stratified by prenatal-care status, the contribution of examination protocol and of access to care is inferred rather than demonstrated; both are testable hypotheses for a prospective, protocolized study.

title: Pacing during TAVR through a coronary wire in the coronary artery and left ventricular wire
authors: Ruisong Ma; Lili Zhang; Wang Liao; Sheng Wang
abstract: The conventional pacing-over-the-wire technique in transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) results in high impedance and voltage thresholds, which may cause loss of capture and valve embolisation. Our team reported that coronary wire pacing, in which a coronary wire is placed in the left coronary artery (anode) and a left ventricular wire (cathode), is associated with extremely low impedance and pacing voltage thresholds in patients who are at high risk of coronary obstruction. Moreover, coronary wire pacing is simple and reliable. In this study, we illustrate the coronary wire pacing technique in a patient to provide a new approach to wire pacing in TAVR.

title: One-stop photon-counting CT angiography for simultaneous assessment of cardio-cerebrovascular lesions: A case report
authors: Yuanyuan Wan; 邹丹丹; Jinhui Lan; Fan Yang; Jizhao Jiang; Yongwei Liu; Wei Tian; Gang Wang; Yanli Zhang
abstract: We report a 73-year-old male admitted for 2-year progressive dysuria, with incidental detection of abnormal cardiovascular signs on physical examination. Initial evaluation via energy-integrating detector computed tomography (EID-CT) coronary angiography and cranial magnetic resonance imaging identified key vascular abnormalities, while subsequent photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT) combined cardio-cerebral computed tomography angiography (CTA) provided more detailed assessment of stenosis severity, plaque composition, and the entire vascular bed. The combined PCD-CT scan delineated synchronous lesions in detail: proximal left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery plaque, ascending aortic dilatation with left coronary sinus aneurysm compressing the left atrium, and occlusion of the intracranial right vertebral artery. Importantly, PCD-CT cardio-cerebral CTA yielded a lower radiation dose compared with standalone EID-CT coronary angiography. With spectral reconstruction, the severity of LAD stenosis was re-evaluated and interpreted as mild stenosis, a lower grade than that assessed by EID-CT; meanwhile, 0.4 mm thin-slice imaging enabled detailed compositional analysis of the coronary plaque, with imaging features suggestive of a stable plaque. Based on multidisciplinary discussion integrating all imaging findings and clinical context, a treatment strategy was formulated: prioritize high-risk aortic lesion management, synchronously perform coronary artery bypass grafting for myocardial ischemia prevention, and electively address intracranial stenosis. This case demonstrates the preliminary clinical value of PCD-CT as a supportive imaging modality for the evaluation and multidisciplinary management of concurrent cardio-cerebrovascular diseases.

title: Staphylococcus aureus-associated infected subclavian artery pseudoaneurysm treated with dual bare-metal stent implantation: a case report
authors: Ruihua Li; Shuohao Shen; Yuanbin Cao; Jianjun Jiang; 丁祥就
abstract: Infected subclavian artery aneurysms are exceedingly rare, life-threatening vascular lesions associated with high risks of rupture and mortality. We report a 70-year-old male presenting with intermittent hemoptysis, who was diagnosed with a pseudoaneurysm of the left subclavian artery adjacent to the dominant vertebral artery. Blood cultures confirmed methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus infection. The patient underwent endovascular repair with dual bare-metal stents to preserve vertebral artery perfusion. Hemoptysis completely resolved post-intervention. Complete thrombosis and occlusion of the aneurysm sac were achieved at the 3-month follow-up, with remarkable sac shrinkage observed at 6 months. This case suggests that dual bare-metal stents may represent a feasible potential treatment alternative for highly selected patients with infected subclavian artery aneurysms. Long-term safety and efficacy remain to be further verified. Long-term antimicrobial therapy and close surveillance remain mandatory.

title: Calcineurin inhibitors treatment in kidney transplant recipients is frequently associated with hyperkalemia, acidosis and hypertension but not with increased expression or phosphorylation of the sodium chloride cotransporter
authors: Ludovic Di Ascia; Jennifer Baraka-Vidot; Cyril Ferdynus; Jean-Paul Duong; Céline Bairras Martin; pierre merville; Lionel Couzi; Dominique Eladari; Régine Chambrey
abstract: Background and hypothesis Calcineurin inhibitors (CNIs), widely used after kidney transplantation, may alter signaling pathways regulating the NaCl cotransporter (NCC), potentially causing an acquired form of pseudo-hypoaldosteronism type II (PHAII), characterized by hyperkalemia, metabolic acidosis, and hypertension. Methods We assessed the prevalence of a PHAII-like phenotype in kidney transplant recipients (KTRs) receiving CNIs in two independent cohorts: a retrospective cohort (n = 172) and a prospective cohort (n = 58). In the prospective cohort, NCC and phosphorylated NCC (pNCC) abundance were measured in urinary extracellular vesicles (uEVs). Results Approximately 25% of KTRs exhibited a PHAII-like phenotype in both cohorts. Contrary to expectations, NCC and pNCC expression in uEVs were lower in CNI-treated KTRs than in healthy volunteers. No differences in NCC or pNCC abundance were observed between KTRs with and without the phenotype. Similarly, kidney transplant biopsies from patients with the phenotype showed NCC and pNCC staining comparable to control biopsies from patients with minimal change disease. Conclusion Although hyperkalemia, metabolic acidosis, and hypertension frequently coexist in CNI-treated KTRs, the absence of NCC upregulation does not support the hypothesis that chronic CNI therapy induces the characteristic molecular abnormalities of PHAII.

title: TO EVALUATE THE ULTRASOUND-GUIDED INFRACLAVICULAR AND SUPRACLAVICULAR APPROACHES TO THE BRACHIAL PLEXUSES BLOCK FOR UPPER LIMB SURGERIES.
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
abstract: Background: Ultrasound-guided brachial plexus blocks are widely used for upper limb surgeries, with supraclavicular and infraclavicular approaches being the most commonly employed techniques.However, there remains ongoing debate regarding their comparative efficacy, block characteristics, and safety profiles.Aim: To compare ultrasound-guided supraclavicular and infraclavicular approaches to brachial plexus block in patients undergoing upper limb surgeries.Methods: This prospective, randomized, double-blind clinical study was conducted on 70 patients (ASA I-II, 18-60 years), randomly allocated into two groups: Group S (supraclavicular) and Group I (infraclavicular), with 35 patients each.Both groups received a standardized local anesthetic mixture.Primary outcomes included onset and duration of sensory and motor block, and block performance time.Secondary outcomes included duration of analgesia, block success rate, Visual Analog Scale (VAS) scores, hemodynamic parameters, and complications.Results: Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups (p > 0.05).Group S demonstrated significantly faster onset of sensory (10.40 ± 1.23 vs 12.82 ± 1.76 min; p = 0.002) and motor block (12.37 ± 1.50 vs 14.78 ± 1.45 min; p = 0.012), and shorter block performance time (5.87 ± 0.94 vs 9.93 ± 1.16 min; p = 0.0003).Duration of sensory and motor block was comparable (p > 0.05).However, duration of analgesia was significantly longer in Group I (1297.80± 71.40 vs 1255.80 ± 46.80 min; p = 0.009).Block success rates, VAS scores, and hemodynamic parameters were similar in both groups.No complications were observed.Conclusion: Both techniques are safe and effective.The supraclavicular approach provides faster onset and shorter performance time, whereas the infraclavicular approach offers prolonged postoperative analgesia.

title: CARDIAC AGING AND MITOCHONDRIAL DYSFUNCTION: IMPLICATIONS FOR CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
abstract: Cardiac aging is a major risk factor for cardiovascular diseases (CVD), and understanding its underlying mechanisms is crucial for developing effective anti-aging treatments.This review paper provides a comprehensive overview of the molecular processes underlying cardiac aging, with a focus on mitochondrial dysfunction and its role in CVD.We examine the contributions of various pre-clinical models, including dog, fruit fly, and mice, to our understanding of cardiac aging processes.The review also explores the intricate interplay between mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and age-related changes in cardiovascular tissues.We discuss the potential of mitochondrial DNA copy number, energy generation, calcium regulation, and DNA methylation as diagnostic and therapeutic targets in metabolic and cardiovascular disorders.The review also highlights the complex relationship between mitochondrial dysfunction and CVD, including the role of oxidative stress, DNA mutations, and impaired oxidative phosphorylation.Ultimately, this review aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of the molecular processes underlying cardiac aging and the pivotal role of mitochondrial dysfunction in the pathogenesis of CVD.

title: Automated carotid artery atherosclerotic inflammation segmentation in PET using MSR-Net
authors: Ran Li; Abhinav K. Jha; Jie Zheng; Richard A. Laforest; Yongjian Liu; Mohamed Zayed; Tyler J. Fraum; Barry Alan Siegel; Malak Itani; Joyce C Mhlanga; Pamela K. Woodard
abstract: Abstract Abstract Objective. To develop an automated method for segmentation and uptake quantification of carotid atherosclerotic inflammation on 64Cu-CANF-comb PET while accounting for partial-volume and tissue-fraction effects. Approach. Synthetic carotid PET images with known fractional-volume ground truth were generated by combining MR-derived high-resolution activity maps with GATE Monte Carlo simulation incorporating major PET physical processes and matched to the Biograph mMR acquisition and reconstruction. A two-stage network first localized the carotid vessel wall from T1-weighted MR and then estimated voxel-wise inflammation fraction from masked PET. Both stages used a multiscale residual (MSR) convolutional backbone. Performance was compared with U-Net, Transformer U-Net, DUCK-Net, and iterative Yang partial-volume correction. Main results. In a two-alternative forced-choice study, five nuclear-medicine physicians identified real images with 54% accuracy (54/100; Wilson 95% CI 0.44–0.63; exact binomial p = 0.48). On 184 simulated test slices from five held-out patients, the proposed method achieved a weighted DSC of 0.79, compared with 0.73 for U-Net, 0.69 for Transformer U-Net, and 0.75 for DUCK-Net, with corresponding HD values of 1.85, 2.29, 2.32, and 2.23 voxels. Patient-cluster bootstrap comparisons favored the proposed method for DSC and HD against all three baselines (Holm-corrected p ≤ 0.031). Overall ENRMSE was 0.24 versus 0.59, 0.68, and 0.59 for the three DL baselines and 0.57 for iterative Yang. In seven patients, corrected SUV showed a positive association with MR-derived lipid-rich/necrotic core with hemorrhage. Significance. The proposed framework improved carotid PET segmentation and uptake quantification under simulated conditions. The patient analysis is preliminary and requires external validation with biological reference standards before clinical deployment.

title: Prevalence of frailty syndrome among patients with severe aortic stenosis qualified for TAVI
authors: Natalia Świątoniowska-Lonc; Kinga Węgrzynowska‐Teodorczyk; Francesco Perone; Krzysztof Ściborski; Waldemar Banasiak; Adrian Doroszko
abstract: Abstract Background Frailty syndrome is a common comorbidity in elderly patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS), significantly influencing outcomes of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). Early identification of frailty and its determinants is essential for optimizing care and improving quality of life. Methods This cross-sectional, observational study included 113 Polish patients qualified for TAVI between January and September 2024. Frailty was assessed using the Tilburg Frailty Indicator (TFI). Quality of life, mental health, and social support were evaluated with TASQ, HADS, and MSPSS questionnaires. Logistic regression was used to identify predictors of frailty. Results Frailty syndrome was present in 82.3% of patients. Higher frailty levels were associated with worse NYHA class, unhealthy lifestyle, and increased emotional burden. Depression and anxiety were significantly correlated with frailty, especially its psychological domain. Logistic regression revealed that NYHA class, emotional impact (TASQ), and unhealthy lifestyle were independent predictors of frailty. Social support negatively correlated with social frailty scores, suggesting a protective effect. Conclusions Frailty is highly prevalent among patients with severe AS undergoing TAVI. Comprehensive preprocedural assessment should include physical, emotional, and social factors. Targeted interventions - particularly prehabilitation and psychosocial support - may help address modifiable components of frailty in this population. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: Exercise for Older People with Heart Failure and Frailty: Should We Even Try?
authors: Sunanthiny Krishnan; Amye CN Goddard; Matthew Annals; Iain B Squire; Shirley Sze
abstract: The benefits of exercise in older patients with heart failure (HF) and frailty are twofold: (i) improvement in cardiopulmonary capacity, thus reducing HF-related sequelae; (ii) attenuation of decline in physical function, thus improving frailty status. Despite the clear benefits, exercise training (ET) remains underutilised as a treatment modality in this patient population. Guidelines on the specific type of exercise intervention best suited for this population are still lacking. In this review, we discuss (i) pathophysiology underlying exercise intolerance in patients with HF; (ii) impact of frailty on HF and exercise capacity; (iii) benefits and safety of ET; (iv) recommended ET programme for this population; (v) mode of delivery and (vi) potential barriers in the uptake of ET and strategies to overcome them. An effective ET intervention in this population warrants individualisation to patient's physical capacity, while addressing possible barriers to uptake so as to ensure sustained participation in the programme.

title: Management Anesthesia of Lumbar Plexus Block and Sacral Plexus Block for Hip Disarticulation Due to ALI Rutherford IIB with Severe Cardiac and Pulmonary Problems
authors: Akhiruddin Akhiruddin; Akhmad Yun Jufan; Farhan Ali; Ratih Kumala Fajar Apsari
journal: Solo Journal of Anesthesi Pain & Critical Care (SOJA)
abstract: Background : Acute limb ischemia (ALI) is a vascular emergency associated with a high risk for limb loss and death. Peripheral artery disease is responsible for 12 to 15% of deaths in Europe. The spectrum ranges from asymptomatic or intermittent claudication to necrosis and limb loss2. Case Illustration : A 68 year old man with a diagnosis of Rutherford IIB acute limb ischemia (ALI) in the left leg presented with complaints of blackening extending to the upper lower extremity. The patient was admitted to the cardiac HCU with a diagnosis of low EF 24%, severe segmental kinetic disorder, LV apical thrombus, LV sec, grade 3 pulmonary edema, pulmonary consolidation sinistra, pneumonia dextra and sepsis. The patient was scheduled for left hip disarticulation. Anesthesia management involved a lumbar plexus block with isobaric bupivacaine 0.5% 20 mL (100 mg) and a sacral plexus block with isobaric bupivacaine 0.5% 15 mL (75 mg). After the hip disarticulation procedure, the patient desaturation until 88%, suplementation oksigen with non rebreathing mask (NRM) at 15 lpm, improving to 95%. The patient was admitted to the ICU. In the ICU, the saturation was 90% with NRM at 15 lpm, so non invasive ventilation (NIV) was used with a pressure support of 5, PEEP of 5 and FiO2 of 100%. The patient also hypoglycemia (23 g/dl). After evaluation with GDS and weaning off NIV, the patient was transferred to the ward with a Numeric Rating Score (NRS) of 1-2. Conclusion : The operation lasted for 3 hours with no pain during the procedure and stable vital signs monitoring. Pain evaluation after the operation showed a score of 1-2 using the Numeric Rating Score (NRS).

title: Tricuspid regurgitation after left-sided STEMI: an independent marker of adverse prognosis
authors: Dmitri Guz; Leor Perl; Yaron Shapira; Katia Orvin; Tamir Bental; Ran Kornowski; Mordehay Vaturi
abstract: Risk stratification for patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) primarily focuses on left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and ischemic mitral regurgitation (MR), whereas the prognostic significance of tricuspid regurgitation (TR) after left-sided STEMI remains poorly defined. We retrospectively analyzed consecutive patients presenting with a first LAD- or LCX-related STEMI between 2000 and 2019 who underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Patients with prior myocardial infarction, revascularization, or significant valvular disease were excluded. Transthoracic echocardiography was performed within 24 h of PCI. Significant TR was defined as at least moderate regurgitation. The primary endpoint was long-term all-cause mortality. Among 1,273 patients with left-sided STEMI, moderate or severe TR was present in 74 patients (5.8%). Patients with significant TR had higher all-cause mortality (44.6% vs. 10.8%; p < 0.001), in-hospital mortality (12.2% vs. 1.9%; p < 0.001), and 1-year major adverse cardiovascular events (39.2% vs. 15.3%; p < 0.001). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated significantly lower long-term survival among patients with significant TR (log-rank p < 0.001). After adjustment for age, comorbidities, infarct size, LVEF, MR, and right ventricular dysfunction (RVD), TR remained independently associated with mortality (HR 2.84, 95% CI 1.43–5.6; p = 0.002). Propensity score-matched analysis confirmed these findings. Importantly, TR remained associated with higher long-term all-cause mortality even among patients with preserved LVEF (27.3% vs. 3.7%; p = 0.011). Moderate or greater TR after left-sided STEMI is independently associated with adverse outcomes beyond those attributable to reduced LVEF and MR. Not applicable.

title: Complex Airway Management in Pierre Robin Sequence with Failed Intubation: Case Report and Lesson Learned
authors: Ade Novita; Ricky Aditya
journal: Solo Journal of Anesthesi Pain & Critical Care (SOJA)
abstract: Background : Pierre Robin Sequence (PRS) is a rare condition with a global prevalence of 1 in 8,500-14,000 live births, characterized by micrognatia, glossoptosis, and upper airway obstruction. Reporting this case is essential to enriching the literature on PRS management, especially in Indonesia, where case data is still limited. Case Illustration : A 1 year ten months old child with PRS, palatoschizis, laryngomalacia, secondary hypothyroidism, and mandibular hypoplasia. The patient will undergo mandibular osteodistraction to address airway obstruction and improve facial structure. Since birth, the patient has shown feeding difficulties and airway obstruction. At five months of age, an echocardiography examination revealed a patent ductus arteriosus (PDA). The patient was fasted for 6 hours before surgery, intravenous access was established, and premedication with midazolam 0.05mg/kgBB. Preoxygenation, induction with ketamine 1mg/kgBB, intubation with spiral ETT No. 3.5 and atracurium 0,5mg/kgBB were given, and maintenance anaesthesia using sevoflurane. Close monitoring was done to ensure the patient's stability. Postoperatively, the patient was transferred to the intensive care unit with intravenous paracetamol analgesic and close monitoring to prevent complications. Conclusion This case highlights the importance of meticulous airway planning in children with Pierre Robin Sequence (PRS) and a history of failed intubation. Successful anaesthetic management was achieved through preoperative airway assessment, adequate preoxygenation, successful tracheal intubation before administration of neuromuscular blockade, and maintenance with sevoflurane. Given the potential for difficult ventilation and intubation in PRS, appropriate preparation for advanced airway techniques and multidisciplinary collaboration are essential.

title: Blood Culture-negative Infective Endocarditis with Fatal Ischaemic Hepatitis in a Patient on Antitubercular Therapy: A Case Report
authors: Mittal Sindhav; Ronak Shah; Parth Shah
journal: JOURNAL OF CLINICAL AND DIAGNOSTIC RESEARCH
abstract: Infective Endocarditis (IE) in patients receiving Antitubercular Therapy (ATT) is easily missed, because rifampicin can sterilise blood cultures and blunt the febrile and inflammatory response, delaying recognition until multiorgan failure is already established. The present case report is of a 45-year-old male in the fourth month of HRZE (isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, ethambutol) ATT for pulmonary tuberculosis who presented afebrile with a two-day history of dyspnoea and haemodynamic collapse. Emergency physician bedside Point-Of-Care Ultrasound (POCUS) showed a collapsible Inferior Vena Cava (IVC), an ejection fraction of 35%, a thickened calcified aortic valve with a mobile vegetation, severe aortic regurgitation, and moderate functional mitral regurgitation. Initial Arterial Blood Gas (ABG) showed pH 7.19 and lactate 15 mmol/L; over the next five hours the acidosis worsened (pH 7.12) although lactate was 12.8 mmol/L, despite initial supportive measures. Following IVC-guided fluid resuscitation, vasopressor optimisation, and Intermittent Haemodialysis (IHD) from day 3, lactate improved to a nadir of 5.1 mmol/L on day 3 before re-rising to 8.9 mmol/L by day 5, paralleling progressive multiorgan failure. Serum Glutamic-Oxaloacetic Transaminase (SGOT) was 7,279 IU/L (182 times the upper limit of normal) at presentation, indicating pre-arrival ischaemic hepatitis, and exceeded 20,000 IU/L by day 2. Two pre-antibiotic blood culture sets remained negative for growth at 96 hours (Day 4) of incubation, consistent with probable rifampicin-associated blood culture-negative endocarditis. The patient died on day 5 after a cardiac arrest unresponsive to resuscitation. This case demonstrates that IE on a tuberculosis-predisposed calcified valve can present afebrile with extreme hyperlactataemia and established ischaemic hepatitis, and that an early lactate-clearance response does not preclude terminal re-deterioration once hepatic and multiorgan failure are structurally established.

title: Perioperative anaesthetic management of EHPVO with coexisting severe valvular and congenital heart disease
authors: Shilpa Sarang Kore; Pritish Vijh
abstract: Background: Anaesthetic management of extrahepatic portal venous obstruction (EHPVO) is chal-lenging when associated with congenital heart disease, severe mitral regurgitation (MR), and pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). The competing haemodynamic re-quirements and risk of variceal bleeding require careful perioperative planning.Case Presetation: A 47-year-old woman with EHPVO and portal hypertension was scheduled for oesoph-agogastroduodenoscopy with endoscopic variceal ligation and oesophageal dilatation under general anaesthesia. She had congenital conductive hearing loss, mutism, right eye blindness, and a partial atrioventricular septal defect with an ostium primum atri-al septal defect and persistent left-to-right shunt. Echocardiography showed a cleft mi-tral valve with severe MR, moderate tricuspid regurgitation, moderate PAH, and pre-served biventricular function. Preoperative investigations revealed anaemia, spleno-megaly, and oesophageal varices. General anaesthesia was administered with invasive arterial and central venous pressure monitoring. Induction with midazolam, fentanyl, and etomidate was followed by rocuronium. Controlled ventilation was used to main-tain oxygenation and normocapnia and avoid increases in pulmonary vascular re-sistance. Meticulous de-airing of intravenous lines was performed. The procedure was completed successfully without significant haemodynamic instability or bleeding. Neu-romuscular blockade was reversed with sugammadex, followed by uneventful extuba-tion. The patient remained stable during 24 hours of postoperative ICU monitoring.Conclusion: Patients with EHPVO and complex cardiac disease require individualized anaesthetic management, with emphasis on haemodynamic stability, avoidance of increased pulmonary vascular resistance, careful fluid administration, airway protection, and vigilant postoperative monitoring.
